Psychoanalysis – Max Wertheimer, Wolfgang Kohler and Kurt Koffka

items.stem:
Read the following extract on branches of psychology and psychology in everyday life and answer the questions that follow.
"Psychology is used in law and criminology to study witness testimony and criminal behaviour. Psychological knowledge helps people understand themselves and solve problems in daily life. Psychologists work with professionals from other disciplines such as medicine, economics, law and computer science."
(i) The study of how noise, crowding and pollution affect behaviour belongs to: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'neuropsychology' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Psychology is useful in medicine. (2)
items.answer: (i) environmental psychology (ii) The branch that studies the relationship between brain activity and behaviour. (iii) Doctors recognise that psychological factors such as stress affect health and recovery.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) environmental psychology (ii) The branch that studies the relationship between brain activity and behaviour. (iii) Doctors recognise that psychological factors such as stress affect health and recovery.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? Activities of the mind such as remembering, learning, knowing, perceiving and feeling, which are not directly observable.
items.answer: mental processes
items.markingKey: (a) mental processes: activities of the mind such as remembering, learning, knowing, perceiving and feeling, which are not directly observable.
options: mental processes
behaviour
psychoneuroimmunology
psychology

items.stem:
Read the following statements about evolution of psychology and its schools:
I. Wundt is regarded as the founder of modern psychology as a separate discipline.
II. Gestalt psychologists focused on the organisation of perceptual experience into wholes.
III. The humanistic perspective was critical of both behaviourism and psychoanalysis.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: All of them
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct. III is correct.
options: I only
II and III only
All of them
I and III only

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about psychology as a discipline is NOT correct?
items.answer: Mind and brain are exactly the same thing.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. Mind is not the same as brain, though mind cannot exist without brain.
options: Psychology is studied both as a natural science and as a social science.
Mind and brain are exactly the same thing.
Experiences are subjective and are influenced by internal and external conditions of the experiencer.
Psychology studies mental processes, experiences and behaviour in different contexts.

items.stem: Read the case and answer. A psychologist studies why people in crowded, noisy flats feel more irritable and helps plan better housing. Identify the branch of psychology illustrated.
items.answer: Environmental psychology.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: environmental psychology.

items.stem: In the study of development of psychology in India, the term 'Indian philosophical tradition' refers to:
items.answer: The ancient body of thought in India that discussed mind, consciousness, self and mind-body relations long before modern psychology
items.markingKey: (d) 'Indian philosophical tradition' means the ancient body of thought in India that discussed mind, consciousness, self and mind-body relations long before modern psychology.
options: The school of Wilhelm Wundt and his followers that studied the structure of the mind by breaking conscious experience into its elements
The method in which trained subjects observe and report their own mental processes and experiences
The branch that deals with workplace behaviour, such as selection, training and motivation of workers
The ancient body of thought in India that discussed mind, consciousness, self and mind-body relations long before modern psychology

items.stem: Distinguish between 'psychoanalysis' and 'humanistic perspective'.
items.answer: Psychoanalysis: Sigmund Freud's approach that explains behaviour through unconscious desires and conflicts. Humanistic perspective: the view of Carl Rogers and Abraham Maslow that stresses free will and the human urge to grow and realise one's potential.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for explaining 'psychoanalysis' (Sigmund Freud's approach that explains behaviour through unconscious desires and conflicts.) and 1 mark for 'humanistic perspective' (the view of Carl Rogers and Abraham Maslow that stresses free will and the human urge to grow and realise one's potential.), with the contrast between them made clear.

items.stem: "Mental processes are studied indirectly." Examine this statement with reference to psychology as a discipline.
items.answer: The statement is valid. They are not directly observable and are inferred from behaviour and reports.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (they are not directly observable and are inferred from behaviour and reports.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: The following statement about branches of psychology and psychology in everyday life is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Environmental psychology studies the causes of mental disorders."
items.answer: It studies the interaction between people and the physical environment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (It studies the interaction between people and the physical environment.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on evolution of psychology and its schools and answer the questions that follow.
"Wundt is regarded as the founder of modern psychology as a separate discipline. The humanistic perspective was critical of both behaviourism and psychoanalysis. Functionalists were concerned with how the mind helps people adapt to their environment."
(i) Which school held that 'the whole is more than the sum of its parts'? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'introspection' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Humanistic psychologists opposed behaviourism and psychoanalysis. (2)
items.answer: (i) Gestalt psychology (ii) The method in which trained subjects observe and report their own mental processes and experiences. (iii) They felt these views did not give importance to free will and the urge to grow.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Gestalt psychology (ii) The method in which trained subjects observe and report their own mental processes and experiences. (iii) They felt these views did not give importance to free will and the urge to grow.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about development of psychology in India is correct?
items.answer: Psychology is now taught and practised in many Indian universities and is applied to social problems.
items.markingKey: (a) The others are wrong: Later phases stressed indigenous ideas and research relevant to Indian society. It was set up at Calcutta University in 1915. Bose worked in psychoanalysis; N.N. Sengupta was trained in Wundt's tradition.
options: Psychology is now taught and practised in many Indian universities and is applied to social problems.
The first psychology laboratory in India was set up at Delhi University.
Indian psychology has always rejected Indian cultural ideas.
Girindrasekhar Bose was trained in Wundt's experimental psychology.

items.stem:
Statement: Psychoneuroimmunology highlights the role of the mind in health.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: It shows that the mind, nervous system and immune system interact with each other.
items.markingKey: (b) It shows that the mind, nervous system and immune system interact with each other.
options: It studies how behaviour is shaped by social and cultural contexts in which people live.
It shows that the mind, nervous system and immune system interact with each other.
It contains old and deep ideas about consciousness, self and mind-body relations.
They are not directly observable and are inferred from behaviour and reports.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: Behaviourists rejected introspection.
items.answer: They held that mental processes cannot be observed or measured objectively.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: They held that mental processes cannot be observed or measured objectively. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem: What is meant by 'health psychology' in the context of branches of psychology and psychology in everyday life?
items.answer: The branch that studies the role of psychological factors such as stress in health and illness.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: health psychology correctly explained as the branch that studies the role of psychological factors such as stress in health and illness.

items.stem: The following statement about evolution of psychology and its schools is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "The humanistic perspective views behaviour as fully determined by the environment."
items.answer: It stresses free will and the urge to grow.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (It stresses free will and the urge to grow.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Early Indian psychology largely followed Western ideas. Indian philosophical traditions discussed mental processes and human consciousness much before modern psychology. Psychology is now taught and practised in many Indian universities and is applied to social problems. Later, Indian psychologists stressed research relevant to Indian society and culture."
(i) Explain the term 'Indian philosophical tradition', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Indian psychologists later moved towards indigenous psychology. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The first psychology laboratory in India was set up at Delhi University." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The ancient body of thought in India that discussed mind, consciousness, self and mind-body relations long before modern psychology. (ii) Western concepts and methods did not always fit Indian society and culture. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It was set up at Calcutta University in 1915.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The ancient body of thought in India that discussed mind, consciousness, self and mind-body relations long before modern psychology. (ii) Western concepts and methods did not always fit Indian society and culture. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It was set up at Calcutta University in 1915.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: Psychology is linked with computer science.
items.answer: Both are interested in how information is processed, as in artificial intelligence.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: Both are interested in how information is processed, as in artificial intelligence. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem: The following statement about psychology as a discipline is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Psychology studies only observable behaviour and ignores experience."
items.answer: Psychology studies mental processes, experiences and behaviour.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Psychology studies mental processes, experiences and behaviour.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.
